answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs, with rewards and voting weight capped by that stake rather than by claimed account count. If audits find fabricated work or collusion, the protocol slashes the deposit and excludes the stake from future rounds. A sybil maker must therefore buy and risk real capital for each extra voice; splitting one stake among zephyr, ferrous, and meadow aliases adds no weight, while funding many separate stakes raises the cost directly.
